newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Caltex Philippines to shut cracker, restarts CDU.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Philippines to shut cracker, restarts CDU.

text.p: Caltex (Phils) Inc, a unit of the joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, plans to bring down a 12,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) fluid catalytic cracker from February 14 to March 12 for maintenance, a company source said on Friday.
The source also said a 35,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at the 70,000-bpd Batangas refinery had restarted Thursday after maintenance.
The CDU's turnaround, which started January 20, was due to end January 28 but was extended for two days.
Of the three secondary refining units which also went into turnaround at the same time, only a 14,000-bpd diesel desulphuriser was still down Friday.
It was scheduled to come back on line on February 3, the source said.
Caltex stepped up imports of refined oil to cover the shortfall of refined products arising from the cracker turnaround.
For February arrivals, it plans to more than double monthly 95-octane unleaded imports of 100,000 barrels. It has already purchased three cargoes totalling 235,000 barrels.
It has also purchased 380,000 barrels of gas oil for February arrival, a rise from the 250,000 barrels it normally imports every month.
The refinery was currently revising its near term import needs.
